correctness.rationale: The frozen RESULT.md proves all n>=2 over odd prime powers and nonzero evaluations a=f(0), b=f(1) by computing degree-d two-point character sums (trivial L=(1-T)^2/(1-qT), nontrivial L=1+JT), applying polynomial Mobius squarefree and inverse Euler products, and Pellet–Stickelberger–Swan chi(Disc)=(-1)^n mu(f). Double character orthogonality gives all square/nonsquare nonzero-discriminant fibres. For q=3 the explicit four-character calculation gives maximum bias ceil(n/2). For q>=5 the Fourier coefficient at (rho,rho) has magnitude q^(n/2) by nondegenerate Gauss/Jacobi sums, with the stated upper triangle bound. The nonstandard determinant- and character-normalization issues were checked, including zero character extension and degree two. Independent direct enumeration of monic quadratics over q=3,5,7,11,13 confirmed the squareclass-bias maximum 1; finite tests do not prove the all-degree formula.
